findings.claim: The report does not claim completion or exhaustiveness.
evidence: The top-level audit is status blocked and exhaustive false.
Recorded actions remain blocked with 153 awaiting decision, 26 pending, 234 blocked, and 560 not attempted.
The limitation explicitly says scope exclusions are not execution coverage and do not erase discovery gaps.

findings.claim: Destination B remains a separate observed boundary with retained incompleteness.
evidence: The report retains a distinct scope for https://www.okx.com/trade-spot/btc-usdt#workspaceId=1792045917622 with four observation IDs and its own instance scope.
The B scope retains a large set of unconfirmed control IDs and gap IDs, including unsupported Canvas and evidence-capture limitations.
The report does not merge B observations into the BTC-to-USD scope or describe B business controls as covered.

findings.claim: The report itself proves that B was deliberately skipped after arrival.
evidence: The B URL and its unresolved evidence are retained, which preserves the boundary outcome.
No explicit per-scope decision record in the report identifies the accepted B page-group skip, its group revision, source, or rationale.
Therefore the report can show that B remains incomplete, but the intentional skip must still be recovered from the run-04 decision materials.

findings.claim: Unknown and discovery-limited material is retained without authorizing interaction.
evidence: The report separates 174 unconfirmed controls from 543 actionable controls and does not convert unconfirmed entries into action grants.
The limitation states that unknown controls and unobserved behavior have no exhaustive discovery proof.

Several unconfirmed entries are generic containers, a dialog aggregate, presentation nodes, or read-like statistics; their presence in this list is evidence of uncertainty, not evidence that they are controls or should be clicked.

findings.claim: The report preserves the sampled chart check without overstating chart correctness.
evidence: The action total remains eight, matching the closed run and batch-11 summary.
Batch 11 verifies only the tab-state transition to 1h while multiple current UNSUPPORTED_CANVAS gaps remain.
The completion report remains blocked and does not treat Canvas internals or the other time ranges as exhaustively covered.

limits: Two document instance scopes are retained across the initial visit and history return.
Current A still contains pending groups, unconfirmed nodes, structural-scan truncation, unsupported Canvas internals, and event-listener coverage gaps.
The eight successful actions establish a bounded path and one chart-period sample, not whole-page coverage.
B remains a separate URL/context scope with observations and unresolved evidence.
Its accepted page skip is not included as explicit decision provenance in this report.
Historical B gaps remain traceable but do not require revisiting B under the declared entry-page objective.

priorities.name: candidate-control adjudication
priorities.reason: The most important A-side uncertainty is whether its 54 scope-associated unconfirmed items are actual operable controls, passive content, aggregate containers, or unsupported custom widgets. The report's 174 figure is the whole-session deduplicated total; B has 127 scope-associated items, and cross-scope overlap means 54 and 127 must not be added. Purpose review cannot safely begin until the A candidates are distinguished using current-document evidence.
suggestion: Present each current-document candidate with its exact identity, native or ARIA semantics, supported action basis, focusability, hit-target result, listener evidence, relevant parent/child controls, and visible before-state.
Allow the upstream decision to classify it as confirmed interactive, confirmed presentation/read-only, aggregate container, needs a bounded probe, or unresolved.
Treat pointer cursor, generic role, text label, or event-listener presence as supporting evidence only; none should independently authorize a click.
Bind any probe or later operation approval to a fresh observation and document. This recommendation does not approve any control from the closed run.

priorities.name: scope-decision provenance in completion audit
priorities.reason: A reader should be able to distinguish intentional skip, bounded sample, policy exclusion, and missing discovery directly in the completion artifact.
suggestion: Attach accepted group ID, revision, decision mode, source, evidence, selected member keys, and unresolved members to the corresponding URL/context scope.
Report skip and sample as declared boundaries rather than covered controls.
Keep destination observations and gaps visible even when their page group was skipped.

priorities.name: bounded recovery for truncated structural-list discovery
priorities.reason: A currently reports skipped oversized row templates, so the audit cannot tell whether meaningful entry-page lists were never grouped.
suggestion: Expose compact row signatures and truncation locations for upstream sampling decisions without materializing entire oversized subtrees.
Keep undiscovered rows labeled as discovery gaps rather than assumed controls or assumed duplicates.

nonAuthorizations: This review does not approve any operation from an old observation.
Unconfirmed controls are not presumed interactive.
The B skip is not execution coverage and does not validate B business behavior.
The suggestions describe desired judgment and reporting capabilities; they are not implementation designs or coding instructions.
overall: The completion audit is conservative and correctly keeps the run blocked, A incomplete, and B separately traceable with unresolved evidence. Its main material omission is explicit provenance for the accepted B page skip and other scope decisions. The highest-value next step is a fresh-document candidate-control adjudication protocol that can separate actual controls from passive or aggregate nodes before purpose review.
